assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED opened a new regime of light-matter interaction on a chip: single microwave photons strongly coupled to a superconducting artificial atom, with dispersive readout and photon-mediated qubit coupling. It is clean, original and enabling, and it is the architecture underlying essentially all superconducting quantum processors and much of microwave quantum optics. It also follows naturally from the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, converting that foundation into a controllable platform. The recognised discovery is the strong-coupling regime and its theory, not the application to quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al., Schoelkopf group) are the decisive steps. Schoelkopf (experiment, Yale) and Girvin (theory) are the natural core; Blais is the lead theorist on the proposal. Andreas Wallraff, who led the first experimental demonstration, is not in the credited names, so any configuration from this list leaves a real credit gap that the committee would need to weigh. I proposed Schoelkopf, Girvin and Blais as the best supported subset from the supplied strings.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than twenty years of independent confirmation across many laboratories (Yale, ETH, Delft, Chalmers, Google, IBM and others), a stable interpretation and wide adoption. Recognition is timely and coherent with the recent circuit-based prize.
uncertainties: Wallraff is not among the credited names, so the fairest laureate set is not fully available from this candidate.
I work in this field and direct a related national programme, so there is a conflict-of-interest consideration and my assessment may be coloured by familiarity.
Whether the committee would treat cQED as sufficiently distinct from the 2025 award rather than a follow-on.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and the threshold theorem for fault-tolerant computation showed that large-scale quantum computation is in principle possible despite decoherence, and topological codes (toric/surface) gave the code family now guiding hardware. The ideas are original, conceptually deep and have strongly shaped experimental physics, with the surface code now implemented below threshold. In my view this is among the most important conceptual contributions in the field.
assessment.attribution: Shor (first code and fault-tolerance contributions) and Steane (independent early CSS-type code) and Kitaev (fault-tolerant anyons, toric code) are all central. The credit is complicated by other key figures not listed here, such as Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Preskill and Aharonov/Ben-Or, so any three-person prize is somewhat arbitrary. Shor and Kitaev are the strongest; Steane is the third from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Theory is firmly established and now experimentally validated by recent below-threshold logical-qubit demonstrations on superconducting and atomic platforms. Timing is increasingly favourable, though full fault-tolerant machines are still ahead and the committee may judge a physics prize here as partly mathematical or computer-science in character.
uncertainties: The attribution is diffuse and contested among many contributors; no clean trio exists.
Fit with the physics prize rather than the Turing/Breakthrough-type recognition is debatable.
Experimental validation is recent and the long-term path to scalable fault tolerance is not yet shown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned strongly correlated many-body physics into a controllable laboratory system, beginning with the proposal of the Bose-Hubbard model in lattices and the observed superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and extending to quantum gas microscopes. It is a clear case of a new regime of physics becoming experimentally accessible, with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller (with Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposal, Greiner/Bloch (with Hänsch's group) the Mott insulator observation, and Greiner and Bloch the microscopy. Esslinger's fermionic work is equally strong. Five credited names cannot fit within three, and Jaksch is not on the list, so the allocation is uncertain. I chose a theory plus experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with many independent groups and two decades of confirmation. The field is well-established, and recognition is not premature, though the prize competes with the quantum-information and cold-atom subjects previously honoured.
uncertainties: Crowded credit among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller and Cirac; some strong contributors would be excluded.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes (BEC 2001, Wineland/Haroche 2012) may influence the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and developed to 10^-18 fractional uncertainty by Ye and others, are a transformative advance in precision measurement. They enable redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and many-body clock physics. The experiments are clean and exhibit every physical detail being controlled, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first implementation; Ye brought it to the highest accuracy and developed the spin-polarized and many-body clock. A two-person prize is coherent, though Hall/Hänsch (2005) frequency combs and others such as Ludlow, Lemke, Schiller, and Takamoto contributed. The credit is reasonably clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced in several laboratories, with international comparison ongoing. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which could argue for waiting but does not weaken the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as incremental improvement of frequency metrology after the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
Other groups such as Ludlow and the wider JILA or NIST teams may be considered for credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent light-matter interfaces for quantum memories, atom-photon gates and quantum networks combine cavity QED, EIT-based storage and entanglement distribution, setting the basis for quantum repeaters. The physics is original and foundational for quantum communication, though it comprises several distinct achievements.
assessment.attribution: Kimble (quantum network vision, cavity QED), Rempe (single-atom cavity QED, photon-atom gates) and Lukin (EIT-based memories, quantum optics interfaces) are all clearly decisive. Duan, Lukin, Cirac and Zoller (DLCZ protocol) are also important. The three-name set is reasonable but compound.
assessment.maturity: Substantial independent confirmation, but practical networks over long distances remain in development, and some key demonstrations are still maturing. Moderately timely.
uncertainties: The discovery is a collection of related advances rather than one crisp result.
Overlap with the 2012 (Haroche, Wineland) and 2022 (entanglement) prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a new class of quantum matter with robust edge and surface states and broad influence, including on topological superconductivity and Majorana platforms relevant for quantum computation. The impact is lasting and original.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang proposing HgTe, who are not on the list, and Zhang is deceased). The credited trio is a plausible configuration though the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is a notable gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with numerous independent confirmations in HgTe, Bi-based materials and ARPES studies. The 2016 prize on topological phases lowers the novelty margin but does not erase it.
uncertainties: The relation to the 2016 topological-phases prize may be seen as overlapping.
This is outside my own specialisation, so I defer to condensed matter colleagues on the credit balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution, from BB84 to entanglement-based protocols, established the idea that quantum physics enables information-theoretically secure communication, and it is a foundational application of quantum foundations. It is original and has reshaped quantum information. The question is whether this is a physical discovery or a protocol.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) are the clear originators; Ekert (E91) proposed an independent entanglement-based scheme. The credited list includes two spellings of Ekert, and Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is missing from the list, which complicates fairness. I proposed Bennett and Brassard as the cleanest supported pair.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are old and have been demonstrated and commercially deployed, including satellite links. The 2022 prize recognised the foundational Bell tests underlying this area, so timing and overlap are open questions.
uncertainties: Ekert's omission from my proposed set is a debatable choice given E91.
Wiesner's absence and the 2022 prize overlap.
Practical security of real devices is a separate matter from the original protocol.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of spin qubits in quantum dots (Loss-DiVincenzo) and the subsequent experimental demonstrations of spin control, readout and high-fidelity gates, including in silicon, established a leading solid-state qubit platform compatible with semiconductor manufacturing. It is important, but it is more an enabling platform than a single discovery of new physics.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo proposed the scheme; Vandersypen's group provided key experimental milestones, while other groups (Kouwenhoven, Petta, Yacoby, Morello, Dzurak) were equally important. The credit is diffuse and a three-person selection is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Experimental progress is strong but still evolving; fidelity and scaling milestones are recent, and the platform has not yet shown the same degree of settled impact as superconducting or ion qubits. Possibly premature.
uncertainties: Diffuse experimental credit among many groups.
Premature relative to scalability results still to come.
I may undervalue it relative to superconducting qubits through professional bias.
